create.name: Stephen Procter
create.bio:
Stephen Procter is an Australian teacher of Buddhist insight meditation and the founder of MIDL, short for Mindfulness in Daily Life, a step-by-step system of Theravada practice shaped for people with families and jobs rather than long stays in a monastery. He first tried meditation as a boy, spent his teens in judo and other martial arts, and came back to serious sitting practice in his mid-twenties. With his wife, Linda, he was for a time resident manager of the Blue Mountains Insight Meditation Centre, in the hills beyond Sydney, and he trained closely in the Mahasi Sayadaw lineage with Patrick Kearney, John Hale and Sayadaw U Kundala. He and Linda now live near Coffs Harbour in New South Wales.

MIDL pairs samatha, the calming side of practice, with vipassana insight. Students learn to soften the body and breath, drop needless effort, and treat the hindrances that crop up in ordinary life as material for insight, helped by a short cue he calls GOSS: ground, observe, soften, smile. Nearly everything is offered on a dana basis: a free online course with video instructions, weekly Zoom classes and sutta study, introductory workshops and online retreats, which he leads with the accredited MIDL teachers Monica Heiser and Krister Trangius. He also gives paid one-to-one meditation interviews over Zoom.

courses.title: Weekly online insight meditation classes
courses.description: Weekly Zoom sessions for the MIDL community: a guided sit followed by open questions, group sharing on practice, and classes reading the Theravada suttas. Membership is free and the classes run on donations.

courses.title: MIDL online workshops and retreats
courses.description: Recurring Zoom workshops that teach the first MIDL skills over four weeks, and longer online retreats that can be joined full time, around work, or for single sittings. Offered on a dana basis.

courses.title: Private meditation interviews with Stephen Procter
courses.description: One-to-one Zoom meetings for guidance and fine-tuning in insight practice, booked online, usually every week or two at first. Open to people who are not MIDL students.

free_resources.title: MIDL Insight Meditation System
free_resources.description: The full MIDL course, set out skill by skill with written instructions, demonstration videos and guided sits. A free member login is needed; donations are welcome.

free_resources.title: How to Meditate for Calm
free_resources.description: A two-week starter course for newcomers that begins with five-minute guided sits and slow belly breathing to build a daily habit of relaxing.

free_resources.title: MIDL Dhamma talks
free_resources.description: Audio recordings of the teaching talks from recent MIDL online retreats, free to stream.

free_resources.title: MIDL meditation PDFs
free_resources.description: Printable retreat instructions, detailed notes for several MIDL skills, a list of meditative hindrances and Pali chants with translations.

free_resources.title: Stephen Procter on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: Guided insight meditations and talks from Stephen, free to listen to in the app or online.

flags: Regional: he lives 'near Coffs Harbour, NSW' (midl-teachers page); the queue entry says Mylestom, a village near Coffs Harbour. City set to Coffs Harbour.
YouTube channel is the MIDL channel (his own system) and also carries talks by Monica Heiser and Krister Trangius; its 6K subscribers are counted for him as founder.
No published email: the site has a contact form only; the private-sessions page has an 'Email Me' link with an empty mailto.
Videos are taken from those linked on his own site (the channel /videos page shows no older most-viewed list); retreat talks are recordings of past retreats kept as evergreen teaching.

Workshops and retreats are listed undated as a recurring programme: the current introductory series began on 1/2 Nov 2026 (left out as dated), and the 26-29 Nov 2026 retreat is self-led with no teacher.
